watch.what: MGM's fourth-quarter report after the close. Beating about $0.50 profit per share and $4.42 billion of sales would be good; Las Vegas room sales falling again would be bad.

briefs.name: Dow
briefs.headline: Dow jumps 1,448 points Monday as member Nvidia rockets 31%
briefs.summary: Markets close Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving and shut at 1 p.m. Eastern on Friday. The Conference Board's consumer confidence report comes Tuesday, November 24, a read on how shoppers feel before the holidays. Deere, which makes farm and building machines, reports on Wednesday, November 25. Nvidia's board formed a new committee on national security and export rules as part of Huang's return.
bull: Walmart, UnitedHealth and J&J, which TradingKey named as safer picks last week, are Dow members whose sales tend to hold up when the economy slows.
The 10-year Treasury rate fell to 4.91% on November 20, which keeps borrowing a bit cheaper for Dow companies and their customers.
Nvidia's board said Huang's return 'poses no national security risk,' easing the worry that knocked the Dow's chip member down 48% from its peak.
bear: CME FedWatch shows about 96% odds of a quarter-point Fed rate hike on December 9, raising loan costs for Dow banks and their customers.
The average 30-year mortgage rate hit 7.28% last week, which makes homes costly and can slow spending at Dow retailers like Home Depot.
Nvidia's internal review of Huang's ties to a Megaspeed executive will continue, so the Dow's most volatile member could swing again.

briefs.about: The Dow Jones Industrial Average tracks 30 big, well-known US companies, like Apple, JPMorgan, Walmart and Nvidia. Higher-priced stocks count more, so a few members can move it a lot.
briefs.whyMoved: The Dow rose 1,447.98 points, or 3.01%, on Monday, November 23, to 49,595.31, after an 8.02% drop last week left it at 48,147.33. Member Nvidia led, jumping about 31% to $165.05 after its board brought back Jensen Huang as CEO, 11 days after he resigned. The Dow gained less than the Nasdaq's 6.5% because only a few of its 30 companies are chip or AI makers, and it is weighted by share price, so Nvidia's lower-priced shares move it less than costly ones like UnitedHealth. Its 2026 gain grew back to 3.2% from just 0.2% on Friday.

watch.what: Consumer confidence report at 10 a.m. Eastern; a drop would hint shoppers may spend less this holiday season.
October PCE inflation, the Fed's favorite price gauge, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern; a cooler reading would ease rate-hike fears and a hotter one would make a December hike even more certain.

bull: The index is up 7.6% for 2026, more than the S&P 500's 5.7%, showing smaller companies have held up better than the giants this year.
The 10-year Treasury rate slipped to 4.91% on November 20, which helps small companies that borrow a lot.

Crypto-linked small stocks were hit hard last week, with MARA down 27.2% and IREN 34.9%, and bitcoin barely rose on Monday.

briefs.whyMoved: The Russell 2000 rose 87.87 points, or 3.4%, on Monday, November 23, to 2,669.66, after falling 7.48% last week to 2,581.79. Smaller companies rose with the whole market after Nvidia's board brought back Jensen Huang as CEO, but they gained about half as much as the Nasdaq's 6.5% because few small companies make AI chips. What still holds them back is the Fed: CME FedWatch shows about 96% odds of a rate hike on December 9, and many small companies borrow at loan rates that change, so a hike raises their interest bills faster than for cash-rich giants. The index is still 13% below its August 14 high, but it is up 7.6% in 2026, more than the other three.

watch.what: Consumer confidence and Best Buy results; weak numbers would hint US shoppers may pull back, which hurts small companies that sell mostly at home.

briefs.headline: Micron rockets 19% to $707.70 as Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips, the parts that store data in computers, phones and the giant data centers that run AI. Its main products are DRAM and NAND flash memory, plus HBM, a fast memory built for AI chips.
briefs.summary: On November 20 TradingKey said Micron hit about $590, its lowest since May and roughly 53% below its peak. Citi analyst Atif Malik said Monday the selloff went too far and that tight supply of DRAM and HBM should last through 2027 and 2028. TradingKey named $800 as a price where sellers may show up and $500 as a level where buyers stepped in before. Micron's roughly $100 billion of customer deals through 2030 were announced in September, not this week.
bull: Citi says over 75% of Micron's 2027 chip output is already booked by customers, which would protect sales even if new orders slow.
Nvidia's board brought back Huang on November 23, which removes a big question over Micron's most important AI customer.
Western Digital rose 13.8% and NXP about 8.9% on Monday too, a sign investors are coming back to the whole chip group, not just one stock.
bear: Startup Fortune noted Micron had no new deal or report behind Monday's jump, so the gain rests on mood, which can flip fast.
TradingKey warns memory is a boom-and-bust business, and an 80.7% margin near record highs leaves little room to get better.
The Fed's December 9 rate decision and US limits on chip sales to China are two risks TradingKey named that could hit chip stocks again.

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron jumped $113.19, or 19%, from $594.51 on Friday, November 20 to $707.70 on Monday, November 23, after falling about 23.6% the week before. The spark was Nvidia's board bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO about two weeks after he quit; Nvidia rose 31.5% and the Philadelphia chip index rose 14%, because Nvidia is one of the biggest buyers of the fast HBM memory that Micron sells for AI chips. About 49 million Micron shares traded, roughly 72% more than a normal day, so many buyers came back at once. No new contract was announced Monday, so the jump was about calmer fears of an AI spending slowdown, not new sales. Micron makes most of its money when memory is scarce and prices are high, which is why its profit swings so much with demand from AI data centers.

watch.what: Fed rate decision. A hike is widely expected; hints of more hikes would make high-flying chip stocks like Micron fall harder.
Micron's quarterly report. Watch whether sales reach about $61.5 billion, what it had forecast; a miss or a weaker memory price outlook would be a bad sign.

briefs.headline: Domino's gets an upgrade to a $400 target, but US store sales grew just 0.3%
briefs.about: Domino's Pizza is the world's biggest pizza delivery chain. Most of its stores are run by franchise owners, who pay Domino's fees and buy dough, cheese and other supplies from it.
briefs.whyMoved: Domino's rose about 2.5% on the morning of November 13 after the research firm Baird upgraded it to 'outperform' and raised its target to $400 from $320, about 20% above the prior day's close. Baird sees a 'clearer path' to better sales because the average order size grew in the third quarter and Domino's is shortening its discount deals and adding menu items people add on. The rest of the two weeks was quiet, and the stock is still down more than 18% in 2026. Domino's makes most of its money from fees franchise owners pay on their sales and from selling them supplies, so its profit depends on sales at existing stores, which grew only 0.3% in the US last quarter.
briefs.summary: Third-quarter revenue was $1.19 billion and profit was $4.60 a share, both above what analysts expected. Global retail sales rose 3.2% to $4.84 billion, slower than 6.3% a year earlier, and international same-store sales rose just 0.2%. On October 30 Domino's lowered its 2026 goal for new US stores and for operating profit growth, citing pressure on franchise owners' profits. BMO Capital also rates Domino's 'outperform' with a $390 target, while 16 of 30 analysts say hold.
bull: Baird's November 13 upgrade to a $400 target points to bigger average orders, which matter because more money per order helps both Domino's and its franchise owners.
Profit per share rose to $4.60 from $4.08 a year earlier, even though US store sales barely grew.
13 of 30 analysts rate Domino's a buy and only 1 says sell, with targets as high as $425.
bear: US same-store sales grew only 0.3% last quarter, down from 5.2% a year earlier, and the CFO expects 2026 growth at the low end of low single digits.
Domino's cut its 2026 goal for new US stores on October 30, and Baird warns weaker 2026 results will likely slow store openings in 2027 too.
Markets expect a Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 meeting, and higher rates make it costlier for franchise owners to borrow money to open stores.

watch.what: Fed rate decision. A hike is expected; more hikes would raise franchise owners' borrowing costs and could slow new store openings.
